title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Albariño
objectives: Know how long to keep it

steps.title: Seafood
steps.body: Albariño is Galicia's seafood wine: pulpo a la gallega, octopus with paprika, mussels, scallops, clams, oysters and grilled fish. Its acidity and saline edge match the sea. It also suits ceviche, sushi and light Asian dishes.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 8 to 10 degrees. Most is best within two to three years. Lees-aged and top examples can age five to ten years. In Galicia, it's often served in a white ceramic cup, a cunca, for local wines.

steps.prompt: Which Galician dish is a classic match for Albariño?
steps.explanation: Octopus with paprika and olive oil suits Albariño's acidity and salinity.

steps.body: Albariño with a plate of mussels or oysters is about as close to a perfect pairing as it gets.

steps.prompt: Most Albariño is best drunk within two to three years.
steps.explanation: Yes, though top examples can age longer.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Albariño suits octopus, shellfish and ceviche
Most is best young; top wines age
